title: General Relativity: Gravity Is Geometry
hook: Einstein's biggest idea: gravity isn't a force pulling objects, it's the bending of spacetime by mass and energy. Matter curves space; curved space steers matter.
key_points: Einstein's 1915 theory recasts gravity as the curvature of spacetime, not a force.
Mass and energy bend spacetime; that curvature tells objects how to move.
It predicts starlight bending around the Sun and time running slower in gravity.
Your GPS corrects for this time effect; the theory also predicts black holes.
content_html: Newton described gravity as a force reaching across space, and it works beautifully for everyday purposes. But in 1915 Einstein offered a deeper picture: gravity isn't a force at all. Mass and energy warp the fabric of spacetime around them, and what we feel as gravity is just objects following the natural paths through that warped geometry. As the famous summary goes, matter tells spacetime how to curve, and spacetime tells matter how to move.
extra_html: This reframing makes predictions Newton's theory cannot. Light passing a massive object gets deflected, an effect first confirmed by observing starlight bending around the Sun during an eclipse. Clocks run slightly slower where gravity is stronger — a real effect that GPS satellites must correct for to stay accurate. Push the curvature to an extreme and you get a black hole, a region where spacetime folds in on itself. Wikipedia walks through the theory's core idea and its confirmed predictions.

related.title: Special Relativity, Gently
related.hook: Einstein started with one strange fact — light's speed is the same for everyone — and out fell that time itself can stretch.

related.title: Universal Gravitation: One Force, Apple to Moon
related.hook: Newton's leap: the same pull that drops an apple also holds the Moon in orbit. Every mass tugs on every other mass, everywhere in the universe.

related.title: Black Holes
related.hook: A black hole is a place where gravity wins so completely that nothing — not even light — can escape once it crosses the edge called the event horizon.

related.title: Gravitational Waves: Ripples in Spacetime
related.hook: When black holes collide, they shake the fabric of spacetime itself, sending out ripples that stretch and squeeze everything they pass — by less than the width of a proton.

flashcards.prompt: In general relativity, what is gravity?
flashcards.back_html: Not a force, but the curvature of spacetime caused by mass and energy. Matter bends spacetime, and that curvature tells matter how to move.

flashcards.prompt: What does general relativity say mass and energy do to spacetime?

choices.text: They curve it, and the curvature guides how objects move
They have no effect on spacetime
They speed up the flow of time everywhere

flashcards.explanation_html: Mass and energy curve spacetime; objects then follow the straightest paths through that curved geometry, which we experience as gravity.

flashcards.prompt: Which everyday technology must correct for general-relativistic time effects?
flashcards.explanation_html: Clocks on GPS satellites tick at a slightly different rate due to weaker gravity at altitude; without correcting for it, positions would drift badly.
